Correct
EXPLANATION

The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

xn+1=xn−f(xn)f′(xn)

where f′(xn) is the derivative of f(x) evaluated at xn.

In our case, we have

f′(x)=(ex−4x2)′=ex−8x.

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

xn+1=xn−exn−4xn2exn−8xn=xn(exn−8xn)−(exn−4xn2)exn−8xn=xnexn−exn−4xn2exn−8xn.

Starting with x0=1, we have

x1=x0ex0−ex0−4x02ex0−8x0=1e1−e1−4(1)2e1−8(1)=0.757….

Similarly, we have

x2=x1ex1−ex1−4x12ex1−8x1=(0.757…)e0.757…−e0.757…−4(0.757…)2e0.757…−8(0.757…)=0.716…,x3=x2ex2−ex2−4x22ex2−8x2=(0.716…)e0.716…−e0.716…−4(0.716…)2e0.716…−8(0.716…)=0.714….

Notice that the last two approximations x2≈0.7 and x3≈0.7 are the same when rounded to one decimal place.

Therefore, the root of the function is x≈0.7, rounded to one decimal place.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x-x)^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{n}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{n}-{x}_{n}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{n}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{n}-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.23,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{0}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{0}-{x}_{0}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{0}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{0}-1} \\  & =1.23-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(1.23)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.23)-1.23}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.23)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(1.23)-1} \\  & =1.259\,054…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1}+\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{1}-{x}_{1}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{1}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1}-1} \\  & =1.259\,054…-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(1.259\,054…)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.259\,054…)-1.259\,054…}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.259\,054…)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(1.259\,054…)-1} \\  & ≈1.259,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=({x}^{3}-x-4)^{′}=3{x}^{2}-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{{x}_{n}^{3}-x-4}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{{x}_{n}(3{x}_{n}^{2}-1)-({x}_{n}^{3}-{x}_{n}-4)}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2{x}_{n}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{n}^{2}-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{2{x}_{0}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{0}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.5)^{3}+4}{3(1.5)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.869…\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\frac{2{x}_{1}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{1}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.869…)^{3}+4}{3(1.869…)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.799…, \\ {x}_{3} & =\frac{2{x}_{2}^{3}+4}{3{x}_{2}^{2}-1} \\  & =\frac{2(1.799…)^{3}+4}{3(1.799…)^{2}-1} \\  & =1.796….\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the last two approximations ${x}_{2}≈1.8$ and ${x}_{3}≈1.8$ are the same when rounded to one decimal place.

Therefore, the root of the function is $x≈1.8,$ rounded to one decimal place.
